title: ウェルビーイングシティ政策デザイン
subtitle: Well-being City Policy Design
educationalGoal: The objective of this course is to learn methods for exploring how to propose a future where we genuinely want to live and continue to engage as a "related population" (Kankeijinko). This is achieved by personalizing regional revitalization, extracting appropriate leverage points in regional design based on objective data, and utilizing generative AI.
advice: In this course, we will learn how to use our own power to create cities that realize well-being, leaving no one behind. To prevent urban design from relying solely on loud voices or a few individuals in power, it is crucial to conduct regional design using objective evidence. On the other hand, to view urban design not as someone else's problem but as a personal matter, it must be combined with initiatives that you are deeply passionate about. Unless everyone views urban design as a personal matter, citizen-participatory urban design will not be realized, and consequently, a comfortable environment for each individual cannot be achieved. Against this background, this course will use Nonoichi City and Kaga City as research fields. Students will learn to analyze their "Oshi", conduct regional analysis using data, and create proposals to approach the extracted leverage points. Rather than simply being dissatisfied with society, we hope that through this course, you will acquire the motivation and methods necessary to design comfortable environments with your own hands. Please note that as this is the first year this course is being offered, there may be changes to some of the content or procedures in the future. Therefore, the course procedures will be reconfirmed at the start of the first class, and that confirmation will serve as the official syllabus.
